A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TreeSynth, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The retained material can be matched across substantial reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original data-synthesis and model-fine-tuning experiments, including diversity scores, downstream performance and dataset-scaling results in Table 1 and Figure 3.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthesis, fine-tuning, scaling and dataset-rebalancing results in Tables 1–8 and Figures 4–8, including appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The original partition-and-synthesize procedure is retained. V2 adds a substantive dataset-rebalancing procedure: route existing samples through the tree, downsample overrepresented leaves and synthesize samples for underrepresented leaves to meet a threshold (Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1).

E1.justification: GSM8K, MATH, MBPP, HumanEval and SimpleToM remain the downstream benchmarks. V2 adds a limited application scenario on SimpleToM: rebalancing existing Temperature Sampling and Persona Hub corpora, extending TreeSynth's evaluated task from generating data from scratch to redistributing supplied datasets.

E2.justification: V2 adds Persona Hub as an evaluated attribute-driven synthesis comparator across mathematical, coding and SimpleToM experiments. The SimpleToM comparison also drops v1's zero-shot references. Temperature Sampling, Evol-Instruct and the human-curated datasets remain; Native Trainset is renamed Vanilla Data.

E3.justification: V2 adds LLaMA3.3-70B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct generation settings and evaluates Evol-Instruct across growing datasets up to 100k. The reported GSM8K learning rate changes from 1e-5 to 1e-4. SimpleToM switches from GPT-4o generation to LLaMA3.3-70B-Instruct, revises prompts and increases the reported corpus from 4k to 40k, with evaluation focused on LLaMA3.1-8B. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New t-SNE analyses examine distributional coverage across synthesis methods and before versus after rebalancing (Figures 4 and 7). Section 4.3 additionally tests whether balancing existing synthetic datasets improves diversity and downstream accuracy. The earlier attribute-adherence case studies are retained in Appendix A.7 rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random-seed values, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V1's unfilled statistical-significance checklist does not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive results for two additional generators, Persona Hub and rebalancing. Table 3 reports accuracy changes from 78.9 to 86.8 for balanced Temperature Sampling data and from 85.7 to 88.6 for balanced Persona Hub data. Retained entries also change: the GPT-4o/Qwen MATH Evol-Instruct score is 45.34 in v1 Table 1 versus 61.10 in v2 Table 2. Revised protocols and replaced SimpleToM experiments prevent treating all cross-version differences as comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical partition definitions and disjointness/coverage conditions remain equivalent. Replacing complementarity terminology with exhaustiveness does not alter them. The rebalancing extension adds an algorithm, but no new theorem, proof or substantive theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: Rebalancing existing datasets becomes a third explicit contribution in v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion. V2 also replaces the headline maximum diversity/performance improvements with an average-performance-gain claim and strengthens the scalability description to approximately linear or better growth.

C2.justification: V1 presents seed dependence as limiting Evol-Instruct's dataset expansion; v2 instead evaluates its expansion and interprets competing methods as exhibiting saturation or instability. New distributional analyses attribute rebalancing benefits to broader, more uniform coverage. Appendix A.8 newly acknowledges that generated-answer accuracy is not validated.

D1.justification: V2 adds a TreeSynth code-access link, explicit size-matching instructions, the embedding model, a sample-routing prompt and the balancing threshold. Appendix A.9 discloses eight 80-GB H100 GPUs, roughly 30,000 GPU-hours and software versions. The displayed SimpleToM conversion template is also corrected: v1 Figure 21 requests answer reasoning, whereas v2 Figure 25 specifies story conversion.

R1.justification: V2 adds Persona Hub and t-SNE citations and explicitly discusses persona-driven synthesis. References to Gaining Wisdom from Setbacks, SciLitLLM and statistical rejection sampling are removed. The broader positioning of hierarchical partitioning against fixed attributes and local generation remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental narrative and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work, pseudocode, benchmark descriptions, implementation details and case-study discussion move into a structured appendix. Terminology is revised, and the unfinished NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: The detailed tree illustration is redrawn and moved from v1 Figure 4 to v2 Figure 2. Results are reorganized into generator-specific tables with average columns and a separate SimpleToM table. V2 adds t-SNE displays and numerical scaling tables, redraws scaling plots with additional curves, and restyles appendix prompt boxes.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's single generator and fixed-size Evol-Instruct scaling reference through additional generators, Persona Hub comparisons and expanded scaling evaluations. The tested rebalancing extension and new implementation, compute and limitation disclosures also improve usefulness and reproducibility. Uncertainty reporting remains absent, and the claim of superiority at every scale has a counterexample in Table 6, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gains.
